title.narrative: Promoting decent work and supporting jobs formalisation in Mexico (EU4DecentWork)

description.narrative:
The EU engagement during 2021-2027 in Mexico concentrates on policy first, using international partnerships to leverage the EU action and leave a sustainable EU footprint in the country. It responds to Mexico¿s main challenges: the overall institutional weakness, increasing insecurity and growing inequalities impacting sustainable and responsible growth and stability.The EU response, as elaborated under the Mexico chapter under the Pan-American window of the Regional Multiannual Indicative Programme 2021-2027 for Americas and the Caribbean and in the 2022 AAP fiche adopted in SSC, is built around 3 priority areas: support to the modernisation and implementation of the EU-Mexico new Global Agreement, address green global challenges, promote social cohesion and reduce inequalities.The proposed action responds to social cohesion challenges (priority 3) by supporting Mexico in designing efficient, fair and sustainable social and labour policies to reduce inequalities, promote sustainable and inclusive growth and leave no-one behind (SDG 8 and 10). More specifically, the action proposes to tackle informality that is a major source of inequality in Mexico by promoting formal economy, expanding social protection coverage and increasing public revenue by supporting jobs formalisation. Priority is given to the most vulnerable acting in the informal sector such as women, youth and people on the move whose final destination is Mexico.The proposed action is an essential contribution to the Team Europe Initiative (TEI) on Social cohesion in Mexico. The implementation of this TEI will be coordinated with Member States, notably France, Germany, Netherlands and Spain and its development agencies. Actions programmed and/or implemented by Member States will complement the EU engagement. GIZ is elaborating the ¿Pisoigual¿ project on social inclusion for equality and post-Covid recovery with 3.4 MEUR. AFD is operationally engaged with the Labour and Welfare Ministry in formalising domestic workers in Mexico. The French Development Agency also signed last June with the Ministry of Finance a cooperation agreement promoting financial inclusion with gender perspective and inclusive economic growth aiming at strengthening people resilience to social and environmental shocks. More generally, partnering with European private sector companies will be reinforced with a view to facilitating labour integration, in particular for ¿people on the move¿.

The action proposed is built around the following objectives:

1. Improve access to social protection by designing and promoting adequate social protection and fiscal schemes for workers in Mexico, targeting agricultural day-labourer, domestic workers, migrants, refugees and returnees, displaced-people, workers exposed to high-risk activities and workers of digital platforms in particular while mainstreaming gender.

2. Increase capacities of administrative institutions in charge of encouraging formalization, in particular, the labour inspection and social security funds.

3. Raise awareness on the benefits of transitioning from informal to formal economy among employers and worker¿s representatives as well as the general public
